title: The Timeline revamp PR added IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint, which fetches issues by caller-supplied ids without filtering by the URL's workspace and project, so a member of any project can change start/target dates of any issue on the instance.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL query construction with user input. The code uses Django ORM with parameterized queries and field lookups. All values are handled through Django's ORM which provides SQL injection protection.

The new endpoints use Django ORM with filter() and get() methods using kwargs, which are parameterized. The issue_filters() function processes query parameters but is applied through Django ORM filter(), providing SQL injection protection.

IssueDetailEndpoint filters issues by workspace slug and project_id from URL parameters without verifying workspace/project membership. The @allow_permission decorator checks role type but doesn't verify the user has access to the specified workspace/project. This is a potential CWE-862 (missing authorization check).
findings.suggested_fix: Add workspace and project membership verification. Verify the user belongs to the workspace specified by 'slug' and has access to the project with 'project_id' before querying issues.

findings.explanation: IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint accepts a list of issue IDs in the request payload and updates them without verifying ownership or workspace/project membership. The @allow_permission decorator only checks role type. Users could potentially update issues they don't have access to (CWE-862: missing authorization).
findings.suggested_fix: Filter issues by project_id to ensure all updates target issues within the authorized project. Add a check: Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids, project_id=project_id) and verify workspace membership.
